conceptual assets.information: The 32-bit state records the ownership or availability of each hardware spinlock, on which software mutual exclusion depends. A bus access can update the state and the response returns selected or all lock bits.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The lock state is mutable control state and line 45 allows a bus request to change it, so unauthorized modification can violate lock ownership. A corrupted or stuck lock value can make software wait indefinitely for a lock, while the state is updated at line 45 and returned at lines 68-70.
conceptual assets.attack: A malicious bus master could issue accesses that force a lock to the wrong value, allowing conflicting users to proceed or leaving a resource permanently locked.

conceptual assets.information: The one-hot selection identifies which lock an access updates or reports. It is needed to direct each lock operation, but no port carries the selection as a value because the address only decides it.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The selection is computed from the request address at line 51 and controls lock updates and returned data at lines 44 and 68, so a changed decode can target the wrong lock. Selecting a wrong or no lock can withhold the intended lock update or status, because sel gates the update at line 44 and masks returned data at line 68.
conceptual assets.attack: A malicious or fault-injected address decode could steer an access to a different or no lock, corrupting synchronization and preventing the intended lock operation.

considered, not kept.reason: The clock only times state and response updates, and clocks are explicitly excluded from conceptual assets (lines 20, 43, and 62).
The reset only initializes the lock state and response, and reset inputs are explicitly excluded from conceptual assets (lines 21, 41, and 60).
The strobe is an access or handshake control field that only conditions the lock update and response acknowledge, rather than information of its own (lines 44, 63, and 66).
The acknowledge only copies the request strobe as a bus handshake, so it is excluded as a handshake copy (line 63).
The error flag is assigned only the constant '0', so it carries no mutable security-relevant information (line 64).
The fields are declared at line 22 but are never read or used by the RTL, so no asset mechanism exists for them.
